summary: X = J_T⁻¹(YᴴJ_T); count sizes in the two products.

steps.claim: Since J_T is invertible, X = J_T⁻¹(J_T X) = J_T⁻¹(Yᴴ J_T) by hypothesis e; so it suffices to bound the (a, b) entry of J_T⁻¹(YᴴJ_T).

steps.lean:
mem_ofSize_mono
  (HasMatSize.mulVec S.gram_mem_ofSize.2 (fun m ↦
  dotProduct_mem_ofSize (by simpa using h · · m) (S.gram_mem_ofSize.1 · b)) a)
steps.claim: The (m, b) entry of YᴴJ_T is Σ_n conj(Y_{nm}) J_{nb}: only rows n with J_{nb} ≠ 0 contribute, and for them conj(Y_{nm}) ∈ B^S_i (h and the involution axiom), while column b of J_T lies in vecsOfSize(S, 1); so the column (YᴴJ_T)_{·b} lies in vecsOfSize(S, i + 2) (dotProduct_mem_ofSize). J_T⁻¹ has size 1, so J_T⁻¹·(YᴴJ_T)_{·b} lies in vecsOfSize(S, 1 + (i + 2) + 1) = vecsOfSize(S, i + 4) (HasMatSize.mulVec); its entry a is X_{ab}.
